label: Findings of the tranche F adversarial review, recorded at the baseline before any repair. Each names the exact file and symbol, the precondition an attacker or a race needs, the impact, and how it was reproduced. A status of FIXED names the ledger record and the regression test; EXTERNALLY_BLOCKED means the repair is a repository or organization setting this environment cannot read or change, and docs/security/owner_actions.md says exactly what to do.

statuses.FIXED: repaired in this branch, with a regression test that fails on the baseline
statuses.EXTERNALLY_BLOCKED: the repair is an owner action outside this repository's files
statuses.ACCEPTED_LIMITATION: a stated limit of the design, enforced as stated and documented

findings.title: a digest-only verification reports accepted=True with no signature checked
findings.precondition: Any caller that reads the verify() report, or the CLI exit status, of a --mode digests run. Nothing authenticates the candidate in that mode: SHA256SUMS, the provenance and the index can all be rewritten consistently by whoever controls the directory.
findings.impact: verify(mode='digests') returns {'accepted': True, 'signature': 'NOT_CHECKED (digests mode)'} and the CLI exits 0, so the one boolean a consumer is most likely to read says a forged, unsigned candidate was accepted. No outcome distinguishes integrity, provenance structure, a cryptographic signature, a trusted signer and an authorized release; the last does not exist at all.

reproduction.observed_at_baseline: verify(rc, policy, mode='digests')['accepted'] is True for an unsigned candidate

findings.title: verification depends on the verifier's checkout, lockfile and implicit trust root
findings.precondition: A verifier that is not the build machine, or a build machine whose uv.lock or environment locks were edited after the release was built.
findings.impact: The SBOM is compared with the VERIFIER's uv.lock and environment locks (sbom_problems(doc, root)), not with the declarations inside the signed source archive, so a correct release fails on another checkout and a consistently edited local lockfile changes the verdict. The signature is checked against whatever Sigstore trust root the verifier's sigstore package or TUF cache holds; the policy defaults to a path inside the checkout. Archive members are read whole with no size, count or ratio bound, and in digests mode that happens before anything is authenticated. SHA256SUMS lines are parsed leniently: a name listed twice keeps the last digest.

reproduction.observed_at_baseline: tools/supply_chain.py at 89e9da0: sbom_problems compared against ROOT/uv.lock; verify_signature passed no --trust-config

findings.title: no contract says which release bytes must be identical across builds
findings.precondition: Any claim that a release candidate is reproducible.
findings.impact: The module states 'the same commit always packs to the same bytes', tested only by two builds in one process and one environment. The provenance carries the run id, so SHA256SUMS and index.json differ between hosted runs, and nothing separates the deterministic payload from run-specific attestation.

reproduction.observed_at_baseline: tests/test_supply_chain.py::test_the_archive_is_deterministic builds twice in the same environment

findings.title: the default branch's AI workflow has no trust gate, and a third-party bot's comment started it
findings.precondition: Comment- and issue-triggered workflows run from the DEFAULT branch's file. On main, the job's condition is the '@claude' mention alone; the repository is public.
findings.impact: Any GitHub account, including any integration bot, can start a job holding contents: write, pull-requests: write, issues: write, id-token: write and the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret. Observed: run 32391406642, started by chatgpt-codex-connector[bot] on 2026-08-20, logged 'No trigger was met for @claude', entered agent mode, obtained a GitHub OIDC token and attempted the app-token exchange, which failed only because the PR's workflow file differed from the default branch's. The author_association gate on this branch does nothing until it reaches the default branch.

reproduction.observed_at_baseline: Requesting OIDC token... OIDC token successfully obtained... Exchanging OIDC token for app token

findings.title: the default branch is unprotected: no rulesets, no required checks, no required review
findings.precondition: Any principal with write access, including an automation token with contents: write.
findings.impact: GET /repos/.../branches/main reports protected: false and required status checks enforcement_level 'off'; GET /rulesets returns []. Nothing outside the AI prevents a direct push to main or a merge without review, and no CI result is required for a merge. Separation between proposing, approving, signing and releasing is not enforced by the platform.

findings.title: workflows retired on this branch are still active on the default branch
findings.precondition: A tag push matching the retired programme's stage-tag pattern, or a manual dispatch.
findings.impact: The Actions workflow list reports release.yml, identity-discovery.yml, reference-backend.yml and source-snapshot.yml as active. release.yml signs with id-token: write on a tag push; any principal that can push a tag can obtain a signature under that workflow identity.

findings.title: the AI workflow's gate covers who triggers it, not what it reads; nothing in the repository held the gate or the signing separation
findings.precondition: A trusted author invokes the agent on a thread or diff that also contains untrusted text (another account's comment, a fork's diff, a retrieved file).
findings.impact: Untrusted instructions reach an agent holding contents: write. A push it makes to the branch triggers supply-chain.yml, which signs whatever was pushed under the CI identity. The system prompt is not a security boundary. The workflow contract checked action pinning but not the trust gate, the permission set, the absence of a PR-head checkout or that the signing identity is not a release identity.

reproduction.observed_at_baseline: workflow_contract.py has no rule over claude.yml's condition or permissions

findings.title: writers decide from an in-memory view and append outside the writer lock, so an honest race writes a history the reducer refuses forever
findings.precondition: Two processes each holding a projection loaded before the other's append: two people answering one escalation, two writers of one memory id.
findings.impact: Both appends succeed and each caller is told its decision stands; afterwards AgentDirectory.load() raises on every replay ('escalation e1 is ANSWERED; answering it again would rewrite a decision that was already recorded'). It fails closed -- no wrong decision is ever authoritative -- but an ordinary race makes the history unloadable, which is the defect EventLog.append_decided was written to close and these writers do not use.

reproduction.observed_at_baseline: second answer accepted at write time; RELOAD FAILS: EscalationError seq 5

findings.title: a promotion names a policy id that nothing checks was published, or is still in force
findings.precondition: A PROMOTER who cites any non-empty policy id.
findings.impact: I5 requires only that policy_id is present. The authority store holds no view of the policy subsystem, so a promotion under a policy that was never published, or that its owner has withdrawn, is admitted and canonical. Policies can be published and versioned but not withdrawn or expired, so 'the policy was revoked' cannot even be recorded.

findings.title: a tool process that starts its own session survives the timeout
findings.precondition: Any tool whose code forks a child that calls setsid() (or double-forks).
findings.impact: _kill_group signals the tool's process group; a descendant in a new session is outside it, is reparented to init and runs on after run_bounded returns TIMED_OUT, with the tool's credentials and its inherited rlimits but no wall-clock bound.

reproduction.observed_at_baseline: GRANDCHILD 2966 STILL ALIVE after timeout kill

findings.deployment_condition: kernel containment where unprivileged user namespaces are allowed; elsewhere the run records that it had none (DEPLOYMENT.md)

findings.title: no kernel-enforced network, filesystem or descriptor bound on tool processes
findings.precondition: A tool whose code ignores the harness's interfaces.
findings.impact: The child opened 5000 descriptors (RLIMIT_NOFILE is inherited, 20000 here), attempted an outbound TCP connection (it failed only because this host has no direct egress), and read /etc/passwd. run_bounded's docstring states the network limit honestly; the descriptor bound was missing; filesystem reads are confined by nothing but the process's own credentials.
findings.deployment_condition: the network namespace needs unprivileged user namespaces; the descriptor bound holds everywhere

findings.title: writers outside the agent directory and memory still decide against a loaded view and append outside the writer lock
findings.precondition: Two processes, each with a projection loaded before the other's append, making the same decision (two revocations of one grant, two publications of one policy version).
findings.impact: Measured per writer at b9b2187: a ledger loaded before another process revoked a capability, egress grant or secret grant still authorized the tool run, the connection or the reveal of the plaintext; two authorities each one call under a service budget both recorded an allowed call; a capability id, an egress grant id or a secret grant id issued twice, or a service registered again with other terms, left a history every later load() refuses; one secret id was provisioned from two providers.

reproduction.observed_at_baseline: 12 cases of tests/test_t2_closure.py fail at b9b2187 and its 6 controls pass; e.g. 'capability c2 was issued twice with different terms' on every later load

findings.title: a projection that refused a record resumed past it, and decided against a history that skipped it
findings.precondition: A record the reducer refuses -- written by anything outside the gate -- lands after a writer's projection was loaded.
findings.impact: The first decision is refused; the second starts after the refused record and writes onto a history every fresh load refuses. A refused load() leaves an emptied projection and its old anchor, and the next catch-up folds new records onto nothing.

reproduction.observed_at_baseline: memory store: attempt 1 refused ('written twice'), attempt 2 WRITTEN; agents, policy and scheduler the same; six writers resumed after a refused load()

findings.title: the execution record was appended unchecked after a tool ran, whatever had happened to the task meanwhile
findings.precondition: The task moves while its tool runs: a supervisor returns it to the queue, or lets it again to the same worker identity.
findings.impact: A task no longer running was given an executor and every later replay refused the history; a task let again under a new lease was credited with the first attempt's result.

reproduction.observed_at_baseline: 'seq 18: an execution record for ... while it is QUEUED' on replay; the re-let case's record was accepted

findings.title: one person's COMPENSATE answer ran the external undo once per call
findings.precondition: An escalation answered COMPENSATE, and compensate() called twice -- by one supervisor or two.
findings.impact: The external undo ran twice on one decision. Nothing in the log or either reader refused it.

reproduction.observed_at_baseline: the second compensate() raised nothing and ran the undo again

findings.title: a read was recorded ALLOWED under a grant revoked while it ran
findings.precondition: Another process revokes the verifier's read grant between the check and the record.
findings.impact: The history states an allowed read under a revoked grant; the separate-process check rejected the run only afterwards, by reading that record back.

reproduction.observed_at_baseline: 'an allowed read cites capability cap-read-..., which was revoked at seq 20'

findings.title: a tool's filesystem reads are confined by nothing but the process's credentials
findings.precondition: A tool whose code reads paths outside its workspace.
findings.impact: The tool reads anything its user can (measured: /etc/hostname, /etc/passwd). Writes outside the declared scope are detected afterwards as undeclared writes; reads are not detected or prevented.
findings.deployment_condition: a read-only container filesystem, a mount namespace with only the workspace bound, or an LSM profile (DEPLOYMENT.md)
